name: Aureline

text: AURELINE. Southgate.
Population one hundred and sixty-one thousand at the last count, which was four years ago.
Keep left on the Mile. Carriages have right of way and know it.
THE LONG MILE. Southgate to Campus Row, one mile and a hundred and forty paces.
Laid across four hundred houses that were here first. Nobody wrote down where they went.
CANDLEROW. The oldest street in Caelora that people still live on.
The city was this, and only this, for two hundred years.
THE GREATPARK. Open dawn to dusk. Kin roam free.
Do not feed them, do not catch them, do not carry them off. They live here. You are visiting.
THE ARCADES. Clinic and Provisioner on the corner. Everything else, further in.
Somebody has added, in pencil: AND NOTHING YOU NEED.
THE SPIRES. Nine of the ten tallest buildings in Caelora are on this street.
Forty floors to a tower and not one of the doors is yours. Try the Courant, halfway down.
CAMPUS ROW. The Meridian Foundation, and the way in to Meridian Square.
THE FOUNDATION WELCOMES VISITORS is painted under it, in their blue, quite recently.
MERIDIAN SQUARE.
The plaque on the basin: FOR THOSE THE WEATHER TOOK. Given by Dr C. Veyl.
There are a great many names on it. None of them is Elias.
ARRIVALS: Stonewake, Tideglass, Emberfall, the Eastern Halt.
DEPARTURES: as above, and one board that says FROSTMERE - SUSPENDED, WEATHER.
AURELINE CENTRAL. Mind the gap, mind the step, mind the Kin on the line.
Nine hundred trains a week. The shed took eleven years and two collapses to build.
THE SUMMIT TRAINING COMPLEX.
ADMISSION: EIGHT BOND CRESTS. No exceptions, no appointments, no exceptions.
Someone has scratched a fifth mark under a row of four. It is not yours.
HIGHWATER TERRACES. Rows one to eighty-four.
Built in nine years for the people the Mile displaced. Nobody has ever called it enough.
EASTFIELD ROWS. Rents posted at the corner shop.
Every window on this street looks at another window on this street.
THE CROSSWAY runs west to the Greatpark gate and east to the station.
STATION ROAD, south, is the way to Aureline Central. Allow twenty minutes. Allow forty.
WESTWAY ENDS HERE.
It was going to go through the park. The park won. That was ninety years ago and the sign has never been changed.
THE AURELINE COURANT. Founded eighty-one years ago. Printed here since.
The board by the door: MERIDIAN DECLINE TO COMMENT. Day 604.
THE NATIONAL MUSEUM OF CAELORA. Free, always. Aurelian galleries, ground floor.
A hand-lettered card by the entrance: CASE 9 IS EMPTY WHILE THE PIECE IS ON LOAN.
THE GREAT GLASSHOUSE. Please close the door behind you. The heat is the exhibit.
MERIDIAN FOUNDATION - HEAD OFFICE. Deliveries to the yard.
The yard gate is chained and the chain is new.

_legend: Aureline is the capital of Caelora and the largest map in the game: 152x120, eighteen thousand two hundred and forty cells, three and a third times the area of Tideglass, with two hundred and nine buildings on it and twelve doors. It hangs off one north-south axis, THE LONG MILE -- footway, carriageway, a planted median, carriageway, footway, twelve columns wide and ninety-two rows long -- which runs from the Southgate in the old wall up to Campus Row and ends on the Meridian Foundation, so the geography of the whole act is the first thing the player walks. Two other arteries run with it (Westway at x20-24, Eastway at x111-115) and three cross it (Campus Row y20-22, the Crossway y53-57, Station Road y89-93). Nine districts hang off that frame. Coming in from the south the player lands in the OLD CITY, Candlerow: granite, soot, cobbles, three storeys and lanes that line up with nothing. North of Station Road the west half is THE GREATPARK -- sixty-three cells by thirty-one of lawn, lake, gravel and clipped hedge, with twenty Kin living in it and the Great Glasshouse at its east end -- and the east half is THE ARCADES, parade after parade of plate glass under striped canopies, with the Clinic and the Provisioner on the corner nearest the Mile and EASTFIELD ROWS behind them. North of the Crossway the west half is the MERIDIAN DISTRICT: a fenced service yard, a thirty-by-fifteen tower of white composite and deep blue glass, Meridian Square with a basin and a monument in front of it, and the Foundation's lawns and gallery wings behind. The east half is the CENTRAL DISTRICT, the Spires -- twenty-odd towers between seven and sixteen rows, shoulder to shoulder, with the National Museum in granite on the Crossway corner and the Courant the only one of them that opens. HIGHWATER TERRACES fills the north-west with nine ranks of tenement rows; the SUMMIT TRAINING COMPLEX stands behind its own railings in the north-east; and AURELINE CENTRAL closes the south-east with a trainshed twenty-seven cells across and three roads of track running away east on their embankment to meet the Central Road.
_plan: Two hundred and nine buildings and twelve doors, and the ratio is the entire argument. Tideglass proved that scale is carried by buildings that never open; a city three times its size had to look three times denser without becoming three times as many rooms for somebody to furnish, so the roof count went up and the door count went DOWN -- twenty-seven doors in the harbour city, twelve here, and every one of the twelve opens onto a room that already exists on disk. Height does the rest of the work, and height is why the capital needed a material family of its own: the modern kit STACKS -- parapet, curtain wall, pier, plinth -- so a tower is three characters repeated up the map and can be sixteen rows tall, which at fifteen-by-ten tiles of screen means a player cannot see the top and the foot of the Meridian tower at the same time. The old kit deliberately does not stack: granite, sash, arch, three storeys, and that is all Candlerow was ever built to be. Walking north from the gate the buildings go 4 rows, then 5, then 7, then 12, then 16, and the seam between old and new is a change of height, of module -- four-unit setts against eight-unit flags -- and of century, all of it legible on the ground with no signage at all. Three faults were found by looking rather than by thinking, and all three are worth writing down. The avenue was authored at fourteen columns and had to come down to twelve: the screen is fifteen tiles across, so a fourteen-column boulevard put every building in the city off the edge of it and the player stood in the middle of the capital looking at road. The Foundation's glazing drew one hard diagonal per cell and a tower thirty columns wide printed four hundred and fifty copies of it, so it was rebuilt as bays that meet at the seam. And the plan view -- not the walk -- found three sheets of blank flagstone, the campus grounds, the service yard and Meridian Square, adding up to about a twelfth of the map; they are now lawn, Foundation field kit, and a basin with parterres. Two rules from Tideglass hold everywhere here and both are now automatic rather than remembered: nothing solid may stand where it would pinch a through route, so every lamp, tree, bench, hedge and railing is stood up one at a time and the whole map flooded from the south gate with it standing -- ten pieces were refused outright and are not in the file -- and the same flood is then run again with all sixty-seven townspeople on their feet, because a person is a solid object and one of them in a service passage turns the passage into a room with no way in. The Greatpark carries its Kin as drawn objects rather than as an encounter table, because a capital park is not a hunting ground and the one place in Aureline that breathes should not turn out to be a corridor with teeth.
